directions.reshapedDirection: Keep the destination (typed command-analysis core, thin hook bodies, declarative policy data) but sequence it as a staged parity-proven migration, not a rewrite. Stage 1 (low risk, do regardless): extract deny/allow rule DATA — rule ids, patterns, messages, soft-vs-hard classification currently interleaved in policy.sh — into harness.controls.json-style declarative records with a generated .sh projection, following the existing classified-bun-scripts.generated.sh / generatedSurface pattern; this alone fixes 'changing one rule requires understanding several parsers'. Stage 2: build the typed core as a Bun/TS module beside the existing harness tooling in scripts/harness/ (types: NormalizedCommand, PolicyDecision), with a Vitest suite ported from the shell corpus, and dual-run it against the shell implementation over the full test.sh/test-*.sh corpus as the parity gate (sequential-slice recipe: one slice per analyzer area — heredoc stripping, path extraction, git-command classification). Stage 3: switch bash-pre/post-tool-use.sh to call the core, keeping a fail-closed shell path — if bun or the core fails to execute, the hook blocks/asks rather than allows — and only then retire the shell tokenizers. The awk heredoc stripper's documented conservative semantics are the spec for its TS port; port its comments as test cases. Update scripts/ai-hooks/README.md and docs/ai-harness.md in the same slices (docs currently document the shell-body architecture).
directions.notes: Evidence verified at pin: policy.sh 1413 + common.sh 708 lines, ~90 functions, awk parser at policy.sh:270-557, tokenizer cluster at 733-965. Marked directionOk=false because the sketch omits repo-critical shape: no migration sequencing for a fail-closed safety surface whose behavioral spec is an ~8k-line shell test corpus, no fail-closed fallback for a bun-dependent deny path, no home for the declarative data, and no split despite leafability=needs-split; 'thin adapters' is also partly already satisfied (shims are generated projections per README/ai-harness.md — the fusion is in the shared bodies, not the entrypoints). Contested because rewrite-vs-restructure is a genuine judgment call: Stage 1 (declarative rule extraction in shell) captures most of the maintainability win at a fraction of the risk, and reviewers could reasonably argue the typed-core stages are not worth rewriting carefully-tuned conservative parsers (esp. the heredoc model) that exist precisely because shell-in-shell parsing is fail-closed today.

directions.reshapedDirection: Do not introduce a new once-modeled edge graph: the graph already exists as each record's `source` plus the static import-closure walk that harness:check already runs (scripts/harness/fixture-closure-check.ts via validateSeedImportClosure). Instead, flip the walkable portion from declare-then-validate to derive: have generate-verify-steps.ts (or a shared derivation module in scripts/harness/) compute each record's import closure from `source` and union it into triggerPaths and fixturePaths at projection time, shrinking the hand-declared facet lists to only the non-derivable residue — runtime data inputs (harness.controls.json, .gitignore, scanned directory prefixes like .claude/skills/), non-walkable files (shell, JSON baselines), and the SHARED_FIXTURE_INFRA set — with a stale check on the residue entries. Must handle: the smoke-fixture tree that cannot run the TypeScript walker (the existing MUSI_HARNESS_CHECK_ALLOW_NO_FIXTURE_PATHS opt-out shows this environment coupling is real), preserving fail-closed semantics for an emptied residue, and updating docs/guides/harness-manifest-parser.md plus the generated-surfaces module header, which document the current declare+validate contract. Needs-split stands: derive triggers first (imports ⊆ triggers is already one-directional, lowest risk), then fixtures.
directions.notes: Measurement verified exactly at the pin (12 records / 158 trigger / 123 fixture / 85 overlap / 12 sources-as-triggers). The sketched direction is right in spirit (derive, don't redeclare) but suboptimal as shaped: read literally it proposes modeling a new producer/source/output/fixture/freshness edge graph, when the repo already computes that graph in the closure validator and the repo convention (single generatedSurface facet + checked-in projections, per docs/guides/harness-manifest-parser.md and the generated-surfaces module header) argues for extending the existing walk rather than adding a parallel model. Contested for two reasons reviewers will genuinely split on: (1) the current declare+validate design is a deliberate, recently-landed plan slice with exact-fix diagnostics — the duplication is machine-checked and cannot drift, so the finding's payoff is tedium reduction, not correctness, and some reviewers will judge an L-sized refactor of a working fail-closed system not worth the risk; (2) derivation couples the generation path to the TypeScript import walker, a coupling the current design explicitly avoids in walker-incapable trees (the smoke-fixture opt-out), and it trades explicit greppable manifest lists against generator complexity — a real copyability tradeoff for a repo whose stated goal is being a public harness reference. Prior-pack overlap CQ25-67 confirmed distinct (smoke-subject import-closure declarations, not the manifest facets). severityHint high in lane vs medium at candidate level; medium seems right given drift is already impossible.

directions.notes: Both branches of the lane direction fail against the code. directions.reshapedDirection: Keep doctor an aggregator of subprocess sensors (its DX1.3 header contract: stream sub-checks as-is, never reimplement them) and make the check list table-driven rather than inventing a new typed-check framework. Concretely: (1) a descriptor record per check — control id (must exist in harness.controls.json), title, remediation hint, command, gating flag, and an explicit protocol-adapter field (tally-prose | report-rc | drift-warn | native-json | inline-shell) — replacing the hand-assembled call sequence at scripts/doctor.sh:801-866; the four runner variants become named adapters selected by the descriptor, NOT unified into one protocol (upstream output contracts genuinely differ, and doctor.sh:172-177 documents why the messageId schemes must not be merged blindly).
